t: Vacuum-Energy Claim Tester — Overview and definition
description: Tests free-energy claims against conservation laws and hidden inputs. (Proposed capability.)
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Tests free-energy claims against conservation laws and hidden inputs. (Proposed capability.) A claim tester would take a device description, hunt for hidden energy inputs, check conservation-law compliance, and design a falsifying experiment. The physics is settled; the tool under test here is the analysis workflow, demonstrated on historical claims. Status: simulated. Capability status: PROPOSED. This database describes a proposed capability, not a completed product. Status taxonomy used throughout: speculative (no demonstrated path), simulated (works in simulation only), experimentally-demonstrated (lab demo exists), independently-verified (reproduced by a third party). Generating a design cannot make impossible physics possible; every record states which status its claims carry. Capability status for this tool: simulated.

title: Vacuum-Energy Claim Tester — Teaching-ladder exercise
description: Tests free-energy claims against conservation laws and hidden inputs. (Proposed capability.)
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Teaching ladder for Vacuum-Energy Claim Tester, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Energy-bookkeeping audits). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Energy-bookkeeping audits and Hidden-input hunting checklists. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Impossible-Design Explorer) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else. Capability status for this tool: simulated.
